newsitem.title: USA: U S West Communications sees future EPS hurt.
newsitem.headline: U S West Communications sees future EPS hurt.

text.p: U S West Communications Group's chief executive officer said Friday he anticipates a "dampening" of earnings growth in later quarters because of accelerated costs associated with regulatory compliance and the startup of new businesses.
The latest First Call consensus earnings per share estimate for the Baby Bell operator's third quarter is $0.61 and for the fourth quarter is $0.62. The year-end earnings forecast is $2.56 per share.

U S West Communications Chief executive Sol Trujillo said costs associated with new businesses and complying with requirements of the Telecommunications Act of 1996 will accelerate as the year progresses.
The company already has spent about $85 million through the first half as part of required efforts to provide interconnectivity access to new competitors in the local phone service market.

Trujillo also said that while revenues for the second quarter were "slightly below plan," he expects improvement in the second half as a result of a number of marketing initiatives that are now in place or are set to be rolled out shortly.
